events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.98 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The trip is RydeTAXI and billed on the meter ($52.08 total, distance component $34.08 for 24.2 km), so extra kilometres enter the fare and RD-2's metered branch applies [F4][F6][RD-2]. The only off-route segment is 18:53–19:01, where 3.98 km was driven against 1.87 km optimal, adding 2.11 km with a maximum excursion of 995 m [F3]; that is a genuine deviation under RD-1, which sets no percentage or kilometre threshold [F1][F3][RD-1].

The driver's "reasonable cause" defence fails on the record. The only LTA incident is a left-lane vehicle breakdown on East Coast Parkway reported at 18:27, sitting 0 m from the optimal route [F11]. RD-4(a) requires the incident to be located on and to justify the stretch actually replaced; the breakdown was reported 26 minutes before the off-route segment began at 18:53 [F11][F3][RD-4]. The corridor's speed records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on both East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard during 18:24–19:28 [F9][F10] — flowing traffic, not the band 1–2 the policy contemplates — and RD-4(b) band evidence cannot exempt a segment on its own [F9][F10][RD-4]. The elongated duration (48.6 min vs 28 min estimated) is consistent with the driver's own added distance plus ordinary evening traffic and does not corroborate a blocked road [F2][F3][RD-4].

No consent exempts the segment either: there are zero in-app chat messages [F7], so there is no driver proposal timestamped before the segment's start and no rider agreement, as RD-5 requires; the driver's after-the-fact statement is not a prior agreement [F7][F8][RD-5]. No rider-requested stop is present in the record [F7][RD-3].

Amount: per-km rate = fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km = $34.08 ÷ 24.2 km = $1.41/km [F4][F6][RD-2]. Refund = 2.11 km × $1.41/km = $2.98 (rounded to cents) [F3][F4][RD-2]. The remaining ~0.29 km gap between the 2.4 km total excess and the 2.11 km segment, and the +20.2 min time excess, are not recoverable: RD-2 refunds unexempt segment kilometres only, and the sub-0.25 km residue class is excluded [F1][F2][F4][RD-2]. RD-6 is not triggered — the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days — so no account flag attaches [F14][RD-6].

The driver's reason for it — a breakdown report — didn't hold up: that report was about a spot on your route, made well before the detour, and traffic was moving normally, so it doesn't excuse the extra distance. We're refunding $2.98 as a Ryde voucher for those extra kilometres. The rest of the fare, including time, stands. Nothing else is needed from you.

DRIVER: We reviewed this trip and found 2.11 km on your route between 18:53 and 19:01 that wasn't justified. The breakdown report you cited was for a location on the normal route, logged well before that stretch, and traffic was flowing normally at the time, so it doesn't qualify as an exemption. No in-app message shows the rider agreeing to the route beforehand. A $2.98 Ryde voucher refund goes to the rider, and a route breach note is added to your record. No account flag applies. No action needed from you.

what_would_change: Had an LTA incident been recorded on the stretch F3 replaced, before it started, RD-4 would exempt it (−$2.98).
Had the driver carried a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, RD-6 would add an account flag.

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows one off-route segment (18:53–19:01) in which the driver covered 3.98 km where the optimal route covers 1.87 km, adding 2.11 km and straying up to 995 m from the optimal route; this is an unexempted deviation segment under RD-1.

This is a RydeTAXI trip billed on the meter (total $52.08 with a distance component of $34.08 at 24.2 km), so the extra 2.11 km of unexempted detour entered the fare; the per-km rate is $34.08 ÷ 24.2 km = $1.41/km, giving 2.11 × $1.41 = $2.98 SGD to refund.

The driver's claimed justification (a breakdown requiring a reroute, F8) is not supported for the replaced leg: the only LTA incident is a left-lane vehicle breakdown on East Coast Parkway at 18:27, and the traffic band records for East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard during the trip are band 4 (30–39 km/h), not bands 1–2, so no segment is exempted under RD-4 (a) or (b).
No consent defence is available: there are zero in-app chat messages, so the driver never proposed the route change before leaving the optimal route and the rider never agreed to it.

The driver's excess-distance charge of $3.33 (2.4 km × $1.41/km) corresponds to the un-remediated deviation; the refund should be limited to the unexempted segment's 2.11 km × $1.41 = $2.98, leaving the ≤0.25 km map-matching residual unrecovered.
The driver's account has 561 trips in 90 days and 1 dispute with 0 upheld, so his profile does not by itself show a repeated-deviation pattern and no account flag is requested.

weaknesses: The driver's statement (F8) is corroborated to some degree by a real LTA event: a vehicle breakdown was reported at 18:27 on the optimal route (F11), and the trip began at 18:35 — the judge may find this a 'reasonable cause' under RD-4, even though the incident was in the left lane only and the traffic was band 4 (30–39 km/h, F9/F10), i.e. flowing, not severe congestion.

The off-route segment (F3) covers only 2.11 of the 2.4 excess km; the remaining ~0.29 km / $0.41 of the $3.33 excess-distance charge (F1, F4) lies outside the segment and is not recoverable under RD-2, and the rider may have expected the full $3.33.
The trip took 48.6 min against a 28-min estimate (F2); none of that time excess is refundable because RydeTAXI waiting/standing time is charged by meter unit and RD-2 refunds mileage only.
The 995 m maximum stray distance (F3) is close to the range of ordinary GPS/map-matching error, which the driver may use to argue the segment is partly measurement noise.

claims.assertion: The trip's only off-route segment is 18:53–19:01, in which 3.98 km was driven against 1.87 km on the optimal route, adding 2.11 km with a maximum excursion of 995 m from the optimal route.

A vehicle breakdown was reported at 18:27 on the optimal route itself (0 m from the route, left lane blocked) — i.e. before the off-route segment began at 18:53 and within the trip window — so the substrated optimal stretch was blocked by an LTA-listed incident.

The driver's reroute around the blocked stretch is corroborated by speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) records on both East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard covering 18:24–19:28, and the recorded duration of 48.6 min against the 28 min estimate shows the route was genuinely congested rather than a short-cut for extra meter.

Because the traffic-incident evidence satisfies RD-4(a), the off-route segment of 18:53–19:01 is exempt and no amount is refundable for it; the remaining 0.29 km gap between total excess (2.4 km, F1) and the segment's 2.11 km is mapping residue within the 0.25–0.3 km matching tolerance and is not refundable.

RydeTAXI is metered, so any refund would be limited to unexempt segment kilometres only; here the billed excess of 2.4 km ($3.33 at $1.41/km) corresponds to the exempt segment, so the correct outcome is no_action.
RD-6's flag_account condition is not met: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so no account action is warranted against the driver.

The driver made no undisclosed route change: there were no in-app chat messages at all, so there is no message showing the rider refused or objected to the reroute (RD-5's adverse branch presumes a change the passenger did not agree to; here the rider's complaint is contradicted by the incident record).

weaknesses: The driver never told the rider in-app about the reroute — F7 shows zero chat messages — so the rider will argue under RD-5 that the deviation was not mutually agreed before leaving the optimal route; the driver's oral statement (F8) is not a chat agreement.

The off-route segment (F3) added 2.11 km and the trip's total excess is 2.4 km (F1), i.e. the driver's meter earned $3.33 more than the straight-route distance fare (F4); the rider will point to RD-1's 'shortest and most direct route' duty and argue the incident at 18:27 (F11) is 26 minutes before the deviation and does not prove the road was still blocked at 18:53.

Speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on ECP and Airport Boulevard (F9, F10) is only band 4, far from band 1–2 (severe congestion), so under RD-4(b) the traffic evidence is corroborative at best and cannot alone justify the reroute.

points.response: Conceded on the geometry: the single off-route segment 18:53–19:01 added 2.11 km with a maximum excursion of 995 m from the optimal route (F3). The dispute is only whether that segment is exempted, which D2/D3 fail to establish.

The 18:27 breakdown (F11) is a left-lane blockage reported 26 minutes before the segment began at 18:53, and nothing in the record shows the incident still blocked the replaced stretch at 18:53; RD-4(a) requires the incident to cover the chosen leg, and the 995 m excursion of the segment (F3) went well beyond a left-lane obstruction on the optimal route.

Band 4 (30–39 km/h) is flowing traffic, not the band 1–2 speeds RD-4(b) contemplates, and RD-4(b) expressly cannot exempt a segment on its own; the 48.6 min duration (F2) equally reflects the driver's own 2.11 km detour plus ordinary evening traffic, so it proves congestion but not a justified reroute.

RD-4(a) is not satisfied because the incident at 18:27 was 26 minutes old and touched only the left lane when the deviation began (F11, F3), so the segment stands unexempted and RD-2 refunds its 2.11 km; we do not claim the 0.29 km residual, which is why the requested amount is $2.98, not $3.33.

The billed excess of $3.33 at $1.41/km (F4, F6) tracks the 2.4 km total excess (F1), of which 2.11 km is the unexempted segment, so RD-2 yields a partial refund of 2.11 × $1.41 = $2.98 rather than no_action.
Agreed, and we request no flag_account: the driver shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days (F14), so RD-6's repeated-conduct threshold is not met; this concession does not disturb the RD-2 refund.

Zero chat messages (F7) means no proposal was made before the deviation, and RD-5 requires the passenger's agreement to be timestamped before the segment's start; the absence of an objection is not agreement, and the driver's after-the-fact statement (F8) cannot cure it.

Conceded that the 18:53–19:01 stretch is a qualifying off-route segment under RD-1 (+2.11 km, F3); the dispute is only whether that segment is exempted, which is answered in D2/D3 and in my response to C3.

RD-4(a) is satisfied: the LTA-listed vehicle breakdown (F11) was reported at 18:27 with 0 m from the optimal route — on the very leg that was replaced — and it was still listed within the trip window (pickup 18:35, off-route segment 18:53–19:01, F3), which is exactly the condition RD-4(a) sets; the rider's 'left lane only' point is an argument about severity, not about the incident's existence or location, and RD-4(a) does not require a lane-specific or speed threshold before an incident located on the replaced optimal route exempts the segment.

The traffic bands (F9, F10) are corroboration under RD-4(b) rather than the basis of exemption, and band 4 (30–39 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard across 18:24–19:28 still confirms abnormally slow running on the corridor; the recorded 48.6 min against the 28 min estimate (F2) shows the driver's reroute was a time-saver, not a meter-padder, which is the 'reasonable cause' RD-4 protects.

If the segment is exempt under RD-4(a) (F11), RD-2 produces zero refundable mileage, so the $2.98 computation (F3, F4) fails at its first premise; in the alternative the residual between the total 2.4 km excess (F1) and the 2.11 km segment (F3) is 0.29 km — the ≤0.25 km map-matching residual class RD-2 excludes — and must not be refunded.

The rider cannot simultaneously rely on the segment being claimed and on the whole $3.33 excess charge: RD-2 refunds only unexempt segment kilometres, and the driver's position is that those kilometres are exempt, so the correct figure is $0.00 and no_action.

RD-5 governs only whether a route change was mutually agreed before departure and is irrelevant to an RD-4 'reasonable cause' exemption; the absence of chat (F7) cannot convert a justified detour around a road-blocking incident (F11) into an unexcused one.
The rider's concession that no account flag is sought (F14) is accepted; RD-6's condition — an upheld route dispute plus a prior upheld route dispute — is unmet, so no flag_account attaches.
Maintained: the driver's 90-day record shows 0 upheld route disputes (F14), so the additive flag_account in RD-6 cannot be triggered even if the segment were found unexempt.
